name: Cambricon MLU370-X8 AIDC accelerator (dual Siyuan 370, train+infer)
memory_bandwidth_basis: Primary vendor source states it directly: LPDDR5, 48 GB, 614.4 GB/s. Cambricon publishes no bus width or pin speed on the card pages, so the figure cannot be re-derived arithmetically - but note it is EXACTLY 2x the 307.2 GB/s of the single-S4/S8 card, which is consistent with a duplicated memory subsystem on the dual-die part. Source cn-cambricon-mlu370-x8.
notes: THE HIERARCHY POINT: the X8 is the sibling of the existing cambricon-mlu370 record and is recorded separately because it is a genuinely different memory and interconnect position, not a bigger version of the same thing. Both cards run the same 7 nm MLUarch03 die (39 billion transistors, first Cambricon chiplet part, vendor-published max 256 TOPS INT8 at the DIE level per cn-cambricon-siyuan370-chip) - so on raw compute the X8's card-level 256 TOPS INT8 is the same number the vendor quotes for one die, because the dual-die card's figures are the die's figures rather than a doubling. What actually doubles is memory and media resources: the vendor explicitly states the X8 'integrates twice the memory and codec resources of the standard Siyuan 370 accelerator card'. Memory goes 48 GB / 307.2 GB/s on the single card to 48 GB / 614.4 GB/s on the X8 - same capacity, double the bandwidth - which is the INVERSE of the Atlas 300I Duo's trade and produces a WORSE arithmetic intensity, not a better one, and it is worth being precise about why because it is counter-intuitive: 256 TOPS / 614.4 GB/s = 417 INT8 FLOP/byte at the X8 card level, against the single S4/S8's 192 TOPS / 307.2 GB/s = 625. Bandwidth doubles but the vendor's card-level compute figure does not, so arithmetic intensity FALLS by a third. The die-level 256 TOPS is the vendor's own figure and the card-level figure is also 256 TOPS, which is the inconsistency - the X8 page appears to quote per-die compute alongside doubled memory resources. Either way both configurations sit far below a same-generation HBM GPU on intensity (an H100 is roughly 1,350 INT8 FLOP/byte), so the X8's advantage over the single card is capacity for train+infer work and a 200 GB/s scale-up path, not a better roofline position. NO HBM ANYWHERE - LPDDR5 on both, so the absolute ceiling is low and the honest framing is that Cambricon's 370 generation is a capacity-efficient, bandwidth-poor design for inference at small batch and a marginal one for training. MLU-Link is the standout interconnect: 4 ports x 16 lanes at 50 Gbps = 200 GB/s bidirectional aggregate per card, which the vendor states is 3.1x PCIe 4.0 bandwidth and which is a genuinely strong scale-up path relative to the card's own 614 GB/s of memory - better ratio than any GPU of the period, and the same 200 GB/s the vendor claims per chip at die level. Vendor's own measured claim (with methodology given, which is rare): on four common AI models, single-card MLU370-X8 performance is comparable to a 350 W RTX GPU, with better parallel scaling at 8 cards, tested on NF5468M5 / Xeon Gold 5218 at 2.30 GHz with MLU370 SDK 1.2.0. Full-height full-length dual-slot, 250 W, passive. Precisions supported: FP32/FP16/BF16/INT16/INT8/INT4, but as with the sibling record the INT4 row above reuses the INT16 figure and must not be read as an INT4 measurement. Software is NeuWare plus the MagicMind MLIR inference engine.
